message.content:
Please run the following workflow on our rhizosphere soil samples from the two sites in southern Germany:

1. **Sampling**  
   • Collect 5×5 cores (4.5 cm diameter, 10 cm depth, including root material) from 3 adjacent spruce or beech trees at each of the two sites:  
     – Kranzberger Forst (48°25′8.4″N, 11°39′39.6″E, MAP = 854 mm, MAT = 8.2 °C).  Sampling in late July after 0–8.7 mm precipitation.  
     – Kelheim (48°56′8.16″N, 11°49′19.2″E, MAP = 713 mm, MAT = 8.5 °C).  Sampling in early September after a week with no precipitation.  
   • Freeze cores immediately on dry ice, store at –80 °C.  
   • For isolation, collect 3–5 fine roots (<1 mm) with adhering soil per tree, keep at 4 °C, and process on the day of sampling.

2. **DNA extraction & sequencing**  
   – Extract DNA with FastDNA Spin kit for soil (MP Biomedicals).  
   – Quantify on Nanodrop; adjust to 1.2–15 ng µL⁻¹.  
   – Ship to the Core Facility of Microbiome, ZIEL, TUM for library prep and Illumina MiSeq v3 (600‑cycle, paired‑end).  
   – Primers: 515F/806R for 16S v4; ITS3‑Mix123‑fw, ITS3‑Mix45‑fw, ITS4‑Mix1‑rv, ITS4‑Mix2‑rv, ITS4‑Mix3‑rv, ITS4‑Mix4‑rv for ITS2.  
   – PCR: first step 20 cycles (bacteria) or 20 cycles (fungi); second step 12 cycles (bacteria) or 15 cycles (fungi).  
   – Controls: nuclease‑free water (negative), ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard (positive).  
   – Receive fastq files; data will be deposited as SRR33458690–SRR33458820 (16S) and SRR33459453–SRR33459578 (ITS).

3. **Bioinformatics**  
   – Use QIIME2 v2024.2.0, trim and denoise with DADA2.  
   – Classify 16S with Greengenes2 v2022.10; ITS with UNITE v10.0.  
   – Discard samples with <8,000 (16S) or <3,000 (ITS) reads and singletons.  
   – Remove low‑abundance ASVs; rarefy to the lowest depth (GUniFrac).  
   – Compute Bray‑Curtis, PCoA (vegan).  
   – Predict functional profiles with Tax4Fun2 (97 % cutoff).  
   – Generate plots with ggplot2.

4. **Isolation**  
   – Grind rhizosphere soil in 1 mL 1× PBS, dilute 10⁻³, plate 100 µL on: King’s B, M9 (20 % glucose), MMNC.  
   – For Streptomyces: transfer 500 µL soil to HNC medium, 42 °C, 120 rpm, 30 min; filter, dilute 10⁻¹ & 10⁻², plate 100 µL on ISP‑2 and HV agar, incubate 27 °C 1–2 weeks.  
   – Fungi: same dilutions, plate 100 µL on MMNC (also King’s B, M9 for some).  
   – Isolate Lycoperdon sp. F31 and Collybiopsis sp. F32 from fruiting bodies on MMNC.  
   – Incubate all plates at 25 °C up to 10 days.  
   – Purify colonies by subculture on fresh MMNC.

5. **Identification**  
   – Bacteria: colony PCR with 27F/1492R on liquid culture DNA (DNeasy UltraClean). PCR: 94 °C 10 min; 35× (94 °C 30 s, 50 °C 30 s, 72 °C 2 min); final 72 °C 5 min.  
   – Fungi: DNA from 5–10 mg mycelium (Animal & Fungi DNA Prep Kit), ITS1‑F/ITS4‑R, PCR: 95 °C 5 min; 35–40× (95 °C 30 s, 51.5 °C 30 s, 72 °C 45 s); final 72 °C 7 min.  
   – Run 1 % agarose gel; send unpurified products for single‑direction sequencing (Eurofins).  
   – Assign genus if >97 % BLAST identity.  Record accession numbers: bacteria PV918716–PV918751, fungi PV918686–PV918701 (Lycoperdon sp. F31 not sequenced).

6. **In vitro assays** (36 bacteria, 17 fungi) – three biological × three technical replicates. Score 0–3 per assay.  
   a. **Siderophore** – adjust OD₆₀₀ = 0.5, spot 50 µL on NB agar, 48 h at 28 °C, overlay with CAS‑agar (CAS + FeCl₃ + HDTMA, 32.24 g L⁻¹, pH 6.8). Read color change after 12 h.  
   b. **ACC deaminase** – OD₆₀₀ = 0.5, spot 25 µL on M9 + 9.35 mM NH₄Cl + 3 mM ACC (± controls). Incubate 10 days at 28 °C; compare growth. Positive control: Variovorax sp. M92526_27.  
   c. **Nitrogen fixation** – spot 10 µL (OD₆₀₀ = 0.1) on 5 mL Nfb‑agar tubes, 144 h incubation; look for pellicle. Transfer colonies to Jensen’s agar; growth indicates fixation. Positive control: Azospirillum brasilense Sp7.  
   d. **Phosphate solubilization** – NBRIP agar: spot 25 µL (OD₆₀₀ = 0.5) for bacteria, 10 days 28 °C; halo indicates activity. Fungi: place cellophane on NBRIP, inoculate mycelial pieces, 10 days 25 °C, remove membrane, inspect halo. Positive control: Luteibacter sp. Cha2324a_16.  
   e. **IAA production** – bacteria: grow 72 h in NB ± 1.5 mg mL⁻¹ tryptophan, harvest, mix 100 µL supernatant + 100 µL Salkowski reagent + 1 µL orthophosphoric acid, 40 min, read 530 nm; standard 0–100 µg mL⁻¹. Positive if >5 µg mL⁻¹ (Herbaspirillum frisingense GSF30).  
      Fungi: 96 h liquid MMNC ± 1.5 mg mL⁻¹ tryptophan, 2 mycelial pieces, same assay; normalize to dry biomass; positive if >0.5 µg mg⁻¹.  
   f. **Abiotic stress tolerance** – bacteria: 2 µL main culture into 200 µL NB with 7 NaCl or PEG concentrations (PEG derived from 326 g L⁻¹ = –1.2 MPa) or pH 5–9; measure OD₆₀₀ at 0, 24, 48 h; plate 25 µL of two highest concentrations to assess recovery. Positive controls as above.  
      Fungi: NaCl tolerance on MMNC agar with 7 NaCl levels, 10 days 25 °C; measure

PEG tolerance in liquid: add 2 mycelial pieces to 3 mL MMNC with 7 PEG concentrations, incubate 96h 130 rpm, harvest, wash, dry, weigh.

7. Plant assay: Set up 24‑deep‑well plates with substrate TS1 fein (white peat 0–5 mm, perlite 1–7.5 mm, black peat 3:1:1, pH 5.5). For well‑watered: 3.25 mL ddH2O per well; for drought: 0.75 mL.
